variants.headline: Assembly votes the government out
variants.sub: The government has been voted out by the Colonial Assembly.
variants.body:
The Colonial Assembly has voted the government out. It is a decisive parliamentary event, though it does not by itself describe what follows. An assessment of {target} should start with the withdrawal of confidence and avoid announcing a successor that this report does not identify.

Our assessment of {target} is adverse. Public authority deserves serious stewardship, and the parliamentary reckoning is an appropriate occasion to insist upon responsibility rather than excuses for inadequate political judgment.

variants.headline: Confidence withdrawn
variants.sub: An Assembly vote has removed the government in {colony}.
variants.body:
A government cannot treat its relationship with the Assembly as a decorative part of office. The Assembly has voted the government out in {colony}. That outcome provides the immediate context for judging {target}, while leaving the merits of particular political alternatives to separate examination.

Our assessment of {target} is adverse. Public authority deserves serious stewardship, and the parliamentary reckoning is an appropriate occasion to insist upon responsibility rather than excuses for inadequate political judgment.

variants.headline: Office meets its parliamentary limit
variants.sub: The Colonial Assembly has voted the government out in {colony}.
variants.body:
The parliamentary right to withdraw confidence has produced a concrete result: the government has been voted out. Public attention now has a clear institutional fact to consider. For {target}, the issue is accountability under that result, rather than an imagined account of the negotiations surrounding it.

Our assessment of {target} is adverse. Public authority deserves serious stewardship, and the parliamentary reckoning is an appropriate occasion to insist upon responsibility rather than excuses for inadequate political judgment.
